sections.title: 1. Quick start (5 minutes)
sections.text: Start the program with Start-NOEMA-Fractal.cmd. It opens NOEMA with your own profile (your artworks are under File ▸ My fractals). Look at the picture. Drag with the left mouse button to orbit around the fractal, and roll the mouse wheel to zoom in and out. Choose Start with a ready-made fractal on the Start tab, or open your own scene with File ▸ Open scene…. Your personal library is initially empty. If you want help from AI: open the AI Studio tab in the top bar (chapter 12). Save when you are happy: File ▸ Save scene as… (Ctrl+Shift+S). Everything the AI does happens in a separate draft. Your scene only changes when you press Use yourself, and it can be undone.

sections.title: 2. The window and the menus
sections.text: The artist view. At the top there are eight tabs: Start, Shape, Material, Light, Camera, View, Render, AI Studio (Alt+1 to Alt+8). Each tab shows only what belongs to the task; Advanced (top right) shows all panels in one long list, exactly as described below, and Simple view goes back. They are the same settings all the time, so nothing you changed disappears. Under Start there are five quick changes (*More detail*, *Softer shapes*, *More dramatic light*, *Richer colours*, *Explore variations*) and presets for light, material and colour with pictures of your own fractal. Each quick change says what it changed, and can be undone in one step. The left menu has eight sections: *Camera & focus*, *Fractal & geometry*, *Material & textures*, *Light*, *Atmosphere*, *Preview & rendering*, *Animation* and *Library & export*. Click a section name to jump there. Hide panel (top left) gives the picture the whole window. The categories fold and unfold. Click the heading (▾ open, ▸ folded). The first time only *Fractal & geometry* is open so that you see a short overview. Under the search box there are Open all categories, Collapse all categories, Open all parts and Close all parts; each category has its own Open all parts / Close all parts buttons for its parts and sections. Folding only hides: no value is changed. What you left open or closed is remembered by the program until next time (

sections.title: 3. Navigating and controlling the camera
sections.text: Rotate: drag with the left mouse button. Move the target point: right button or Shift+drag. Zoom (dolly): the mouse wheel. Fine control: Shift or Ctrl + the mouse wheel. Focus: double-click a detail and it becomes the new centre for rotation and sharpness. The section Camera & focus has *Fly through the fractal*, lens buttons (18, 24, 35, 50, 85, 100 mm), Reset camera and four saved camera views (Save camera view 1–4, Fetch camera view 1–4). Camera / composition controls the picture format and the crop. If you change the format the frame changes, not the fractal itself. Focus and depth of field (DOF): click Focus here and then the picture, or choose Deep / Moderate / Shallow / Very shallow. DOF from navigation focus takes the sharpness from what you last focused on. Depth of field makes the preview slower and is not verified together with Geometry Detail. Exercise: open an artwork, press Reset camera, choose 85 mm, double-click an interesting detail and save the view with Save camera view 1.

sections.title: 4. Formulas, parameters and colours
sections.text: Fractal & geometry shows the formula chain. Each step has a formula (for example *Mandelbulb*), a number of iterations and its own Parameters. Drag the sliders and the picture updates directly. ＋ Add formula adds a step (at most eight). The arrows move steps up and down, Remove step removes one. Change formula in step changes the formula. Favourite marks a formula. In the formula picker a small picture shows what the formula gives when you choose it (its own default scene). A transform (a formula that only moves the point) is shown behind a fixed default formula, which is stated on the picture ("on Ikenaga bulb" and similar), so that you see what it does to a known shape. The pictures are finished files: the picker renders and compiles nothing, and a picture is fetched only when the row becomes visible. Safety of the distance estimate: mixtures where an IFS formula (folding and a fixed scale) is combined with another distance model, and interpolation of IFS formulas, are rejected with an explanation, because no safe distance estimate exists for them. Use a group execution or sequence/alternation instead. Randomise a new chain creates a random combination. Import MB3D preset reads a Mandelbulb 3D preset (maps parameters, no code); Undo MB3D import takes it back. The author and the source of a formula are shown in the program and follow saved scenes. sections.title: 5. Material and PBR maps
sections.text: The material has *metal*, *roughness* and *reflectivity*. Low roughness gives a shiny surface, high gives matt. Metal 1 gives a metallic surface. Texture set · PBR puts picture maps on the surface: colour (baseColor), roughness, metal (metallic), occlusion (ao), emission as well as normal and height. Choose maps… reads several maps at once and suggests the right channel from the file name (for example *diff*, *rough*, *nor_gl*). Texture size (scale) states how many times the maps repeat per unit. All maps in a material share the scale so that they stay aligned. Texture size: reset to 1 resets it. Material library… (the File menu or in *Material & textures*) saves and fetches materials. Click a material to try it in the picture; Apply material does it for real, Restore original takes it back. Undo apply undoes. It works the same way for the whole fractal and for a chosen scene object (under *Scene objects*, choose Object material: own). Why does it sometimes look as if nothing happened? The colour of the surface comes from the colour gradient, and the colour of the material (and the colour map) is multiplied with it. A light material on an orange gradient therefore looks almost unchanged. The library says so and offers Apply with the colour of the material itself, which sets *Influence of the orbit colour* to 0 %. You can also lower it yourself under *Material*. Surface Detail (

sections.title: 6. Gradient and Material gradient
sections.text: The gradient is the colour field in Material & textures. Click in the field to add a colour stop; drag to move; Remove colour stop removes one. The colour is chosen with the colour box or a hex code. Material gradient: choose a stop and click Choose from the material library…. There you find your saved materials, those you fetched from Poly Haven (the Poly Haven tab, where you can also fetch new ones) and search. Choose a material and click Use for the chosen colour stop: the stop becomes a material stop with the whole material, all picture maps and the source and license of Poly Haven, and it then works without a network. It can be undone with Undo. The short list under the button has the same materials (and the built-in ones) for quick choices.    Note: a colour map is multiplied with the colour of the stop itself. If the stop is dark or coloured, the own colours of the material become weak; the button Make the colour of the stop white releases it.    Result: the material is blended in. Then the metal, roughness, reflectivity, tone and the picture maps (colour, roughness, metal, occlusion) of the material are blended along the gradient – for example *stone that slowly becomes polished bronze*. sections.title: 7. Poly Haven – free materials
sections.text: Poly Haven (polyhaven.com) has free PBR materials under the license CC0. NOEMA always shows "Powered by Poly Haven" and preserves the author and the link in the material. File ▸ Material library… and choose the Poly Haven tab. Search (for example *rock*, *moss*, *metal*), choose a category and a resolution (1k is recommended). Click a material: you see a preview, which maps it really has (colour, roughness, metal, occlusion, normal) and which are not blended in gradients. Not all materials have all maps. Fetch … and put in My materials fetches the files (a few MB) and puts the material in your library. Then click it under My materials to try it and Apply material. Offline: fetched materials lie in a local cache and in your library. They work without a network. Remove from the cache frees space (the material in *My materials* remains). The normal map is fetched but turned off (the orientation is not verified). Displacement is not imported. The program only contacts the official addresses of Poly Haven, checks the downloads (size and checksum) and sends nothing about you or your artworks.

sections.title: 8. Light, shadows, atmosphere and Artist Looks
sections.text: Light: + Directional (like the sun), + Point (like a lamp) and + Spot (spotlight) add lights (at most 8). Each light has colour, strength, direction/position and shadows (none, hard, soft). Ambient light gives an even base lighting. Light rigs place several lights starting from the camera (Subdued, Normal, Strong, Very strong, Use rig). Looks (material, light and fog): a *Look* is a saved mood. Save Look, Export Looks…, Import Looks…; Restore original and Undo apply take back a Look you tried. Atmosphere: fog (colour, density, start) and sky/environment. Search *fog* or *environment* with Ctrl+K. Depth of field (chapter 3) belongs to the camera.

sections.title: 9. Display modes and final rendering
sections.text: NOEMA has four display modes. The box above the picture (the View tab) has a button for each, and under the buttons there is a short explanation of the mode you chose. Click an active mode again to go back to Explore. F1–F4 choose the modes in this order from any tab. Explore: the fast ordinary viewport, for moving the camera and feeling the shape. The light is simplified and the picture is not final quality. Best when you look for a good view. The quality is chosen with *Viewport* next to the buttons. Create: build and experiment. Change formulas, parameters, material, colour, light, objects, glass, cut and displacement and see the result directly, without waiting. The lighting is simplified (see the section *Create* further down). Best when you create. Inspect: the same surface as in the final picture, and light, shadows and materials can be adjusted without anything being recomputed; the picture gets cleaner with every sample. Best for heavy fractals and when you fine-tune the look. Final Preview: as close to the final render as possible: the same geometry, reflections and refinement as the final picture (the hit limits are recalculated from the size of the real final picture), but with a size of its own (512, 768 or 1024 px) and a sample count of its own. sections.title: 10. Geometry Detail and its limits
sections.text: Geometry Detail gives extra fine surface geometry with double precision. It only works for certain formula chains. The program says why when it does not work (for example "scene objects are part of it", "transport/GI", "depth of field", "normal map", "textured gradient") and what you can do instead: High detail (Float32) – not Geometry Detail works for all formulas. The previews always run with Geometry Detail off.

sections.title: 11. Saving, library, import and export
sections.text: Save scene as… writes a .scene.json with everything: formulas, colours, material (embedded pictures), light, camera and source references. Scenes with Poly Haven maps can be several MB. File ▸ My fractals is the library of your artworks and thumbnails. Save picture preset puts the current view there. Save as preset / Save to file saves the formula chain. Import library… / Export library… moves whole libraries as a backup. Show library folder opens the folder. Library & export: glTF (.glb) and JSON for export, Create variations, Save scene. Never open a scene file you do not trust without understanding that it only contains data (no programs), but large pictures take memory.

sections.title: 12. Creating with AI
sections.text: Open the AI Studio tab. The panel Conversation with AI has: Provider and Model (recommended models have ★ and show whether they can do tools and pictures). Change between attempts when you want. Four modes: Create for me (the AI tries several ideas itself, at most about ten pictures), Explore shape (the AI tries different formula chains in 2–3 drafts and compares them, see below), Create together (a few steps at a time and a question to you), Teach me (the AI explains and changes nothing; Show as example gives a small example in a draft). Budget: limits for the number of tool calls, pictures, time and tokens, so that the AI does not run away. Choose reference picture…: a picture as inspiration for mood, colour, material and composition. It is sent to the AI service only when you press Send (a downscaled copy, never saved). The AI does not rebuild the exact 3D shape of the picture; NOEMA is a fractal engine. Let the AI search and fetch Poly Haven materials: off at every start. Turn it on if you want the AI to be allowed to fetch materials (at most 20 searches and 6 downloads per session). How you work: Write what you want, for example *"Make the picture warmer and more dramatic, with stone and bronze"*, and press Send. sections.title: 13. Troubleshooting
sections.text: The picture is black or the program says the graphics card is missing: NOEMA needs WebGPU. Open Help ▸ About / graphics status. Update the graphics driver and close other programs that use a lot of graphics memory. The preview is slow: choose Explore or Fast 512 px and 1 sample; turn off depth of field; the first picture after a change takes longer (the shader is compiled). Poly Haven says offline: the saved catalogue is shown; already fetched materials work. Check the network and the firewall. "Key missing" / the AI does not answer: connect the key (chapter 12) and press Test connection. 401/403 means a wrong or inactive key, 429 out of credit or too many calls, 404 that the model does not exist. The AI changed nothing in my scene: that is intended; look at the draft and press Use. Geometry Detail cannot be turned on: read the explanation in the program (chapter 10). The scene is large: pictures from materials are embedded. Use a lower resolution (1k) or fewer materials. Help to report a problem: Help ▸ Export feedback (local)… creates a file that you see yourself before it is saved. Nothing is sent automatically.
